candidates.failure_scenario: A package was measured (e.g. Deposit Max 1.4M, Calls 12, or valopers.Register raised to 165.9M). On the next read the indexer answers each band in ~3.2 s, under its 4 s client timeout; after three bands indexer.recent breaks on minWindowBudget and returns 0 rows with ErrPartial. read() stores gasUseEntry{uses: {}, expires: now+gasUseTTL}: lookup reports it fresh for 5 min, get returns no use, and NewTxGas falls back to TxGasWanted. Fast mode loses its lowered fee; a function measured above 10 M goes back to 10 M in both modes, so the copied command fails its dry run/simulation and the user has no figure to raise -gas-wanted to (the pre-PR command asked 1,000 M). A hard error on the same read keeps the last measure, so only the slow-but-answering indexer drops it.

In production net/http cancels r.Context() as soon as ServeHTTP returns, and get never waits, so every background read is cancelled with the page that started it and no package is ever measured; the suite stays green because stubRecent.recent takes `_ context.Context` and no test cancels the ctx it hands get.

candidates.summary: No test pins queryGasPrice's context.WithoutCancel: gasCaller.SendRequest ignores its ctx, so the stale-while-revalidate refresh and the shared first read stay green when the request context is passed through
candidates.failure_scenario: Mutate `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` to `ctx` in queryGasPrice. The background refresh runs on the request context, which net/http cancels once the page is written, so the refresh fails and the price is never renewed past the first read; the first read is cut short for every waiter when its leader leaves. TestGasPriceFirstReadLeavesOnCancel cancels after the slot is acquired and gasCaller.SendRequest takes `_ context.Context`, so it still sees the read land.

candidates.summary: GasPrice serves the last good price with no bound on its age: a refresh that keeps failing resets gasAt and keeps gasOK, so an hours-old price is shown as current with Estimated false
candidates.failure_scenario: The node answers auth/gasprice once, then every refresh times out on a saturated rpcSlots pool or the node lags; each failure sets gasAt=now and leaves gasPrice in place, so the page prices the copied command at the old figure indefinitely and nothing on the page says so. With x3 headroom and CheckTx rejecting a short fee for free, the cost is a rejected broadcast, not funds.
